project.name: ColdStart Killer
project.description: ColdStart Killer is a MongoDB Hackathon project for bootstrapping retrieval for brand-new ecommerce products. It combines LLM-generated HyPE queries and propositions, hybrid vector and BM25 retrieval in MongoDB Atlas, a FastAPI backend, a React and Vite demo frontend, and evaluation reporting across multiple search variants. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start here because the graph did not expose a single canonical runtime entry point, and the README is the clearest onboarding surface. It frames ColdStart Killer as a website-first demo that combines offline LLM enrichment, MongoDB hybrid retrieval, a thin FastAPI backend, a React frontend, and evaluation reporting. Read it as the product narrative that the rest of the tour will map onto concrete implementation layers.

tour.title: Runtime Skeleton
tour.description: Once you know the project story, these files show how the live system is assembled. app.py bootstraps the FastAPI service and registers the shopper-facing modules, config.py centralizes environment flags and scoring thresholds, and mongodb.py isolates Atlas access behind small helpers. Together they define the runtime skeleton that every API, recommendation, and evaluation surface depends on.

tour.title: LLM Retrieval Assets
tour.description: Before any shopper query runs, the repository manufactures cold-start retrieval assets offline. The prompt templates define the structure of HyPE queries and grounded propositions, while llm_hype.py and llm_propositions.py validate model responses and fall back when generation is weak. build_item_hype_profiles.py turns that generated material into item-side documents that the search stack can actually retrieve against.
tour.languageLesson: Prompt templates become far more reliable when they are treated as contracts instead of plain instructions. Requiring structured JSON output and validating it immediately in code gives the pipeline deterministic downstream behavior even when the LLM itself is noisy.

tour.title: Hybrid Search Core
tour.description: Building on the generated assets from Step 3, the retrieval core turns a shopper query into explainable MongoDB results. query_processor.py normalizes buyer intent, embeddings.py produces vector inputs, and search_pipeline.py fuses vector and BM25 channels with hard filters inside Atlas. retrieval_output.py and the shared schemas keep the result contract stable enough for both live APIs and evaluation runs.
tour.languageLesson: MongoDB aggregation pipelines work well for hybrid retrieval because each stage can own one concern: candidate generation, filtering, score fusion, or output shaping. Keeping those stages explicit also makes it easier to create ablation variants later for evaluation.

tour.title: Thin API Surfaces
tour.description: The HTTP layer is intentionally thin: these route modules mostly validate requests, enforce policy, and hand off to deeper services. request_guards.py centralizes privacy and admin rules, while the search, feed, item, and onboarding routes expose the user-facing demo surfaces described in the README. This is the clean boundary between transport concerns and the underlying cold-start logic.

tour.title: Behavior To Profiles
tour.description: After the API accepts requests, the project starts learning from shopper behavior. routes_events.py and event_logger.py capture impressions and interactions safely, signal_builder.py aggregates them into reusable features, profile_builder.py turns those features into user profiles, and onboarding.py seeds that process for brand-new shoppers. This is the bridge from a zero-history user to the personalized recommendation logic that follows.

tour.title: Recommendation Assembly
tour.description: With profiles and behavior in place, the recommendation layer decides what a shopper should see next. candidate_sources.py assembles inputs from profiles, semantic neighbors, collaborative filtering, and fallback catalog slices, item_item_cf.py maintains the collaborative graph, and the homepage, search, and similar-products services package those candidates for each surface. This is where the code stops being generic retrieval and becomes the demo's personalized experience.

tour.title: Ranking And Explanations
tour.description: The previous step produces candidate items; this step decides how to rank and explain them. scoring.py blends query relevance, affinity, and cold-start heuristics, diversity.py prevents the top results from collapsing into one narrow slice, explanations.py turns evidence into badges and text, and recommendation/schemas.py keeps stored artifacts and payloads consistent. If you want to understand why a result looks the way it does in the UI, this is the most important internal stop.
tour.languageLesson: This layer is a good example of separating ranking logic from presentation logic. The scorer produces reusable numeric evidence, and the explanation builder translates that evidence into user-facing language without forcing the UI to understand the ranking internals.

tour.title: Evaluation Loop
tour.description: The evaluation layer checks whether the architecture described in the README actually holds up under measurement. evaluation/README.md explains the workflow, dataset.py loads the seeded queries and judgments into strongly validated structures from contracts.py, run_evaluation.py executes the search-variant pipeline, and routes_evaluation.py exposes persisted runs back to the demo. This gives the project a reproducible way to compare variants instead of relying on anecdotal screenshots.

tour.title: Frontend Demo Experience
tour.description: Finally, the React demo turns all of the backend machinery into the website-first walkthrough the README recommends. App.tsx defines the guarded route tree, api.ts mirrors the backend contracts, experience.tsx preserves shopper and session context across pages, HomePage.tsx shows the recommendation surfaces in action, and DESIGN.md explains the editorial visual system used to present them. End the tour here to see how retrieval, personalization, and evaluation become one coherent demo experience.
tour.languageLesson: React context is doing session orchestration here rather than business logic. Keeping the active shopper and impression bookkeeping in a shared provider lets routed pages coordinate analytics without duplicating state or threading props through the entire app.
